_comment: Template. Copy to catalog.json (same directory) and replace with patterns mined from your own code reviews. Three generic entries below show the schema; see SKILL.md for the field table.

patterns.title: Duplicated source of truth: the same constant or data drifting across files
patterns.symptom: One value (a path, a threshold, a model name, a line-length limit) is hardcoded separately in several files or duplicated between a .sh / .ps1 / .cmd trio; editing one place leaves the others on the old value, so results stop being reproducible.
patterns.detect: grep the same magic number / path / regex across modules; duplicated copies of a function instead of a shared import; parallel configs (setup.cfg vs pyproject.toml, two CI workflows) pinning different versions.
patterns.avoid: Single source of truth: one config or module that everything reads or imports; if a value must exist in two ecosystems, generate one from the other and assert equality in a test.
patterns.counterexample: NOT a finding when the two values are independent by design and a comment says so, or when one copy is a vendored snapshot pinned deliberately.

patterns.title: Long payload passed as a command-line argument instead of stdin
patterns.symptom: A prompt, file list or JSON blob is interpolated into the command line; past a platform limit (~8k chars on Windows CreateProcess, ~128k-2M on Linux ARG_MAX) the call fails with an opaque OS error, and only for large inputs — so it passes every small test.
patterns.detect: subprocess/Start-Process/backtick invocations whose argument is built from a variable of unbounded length (file contents, joined list, LLM prompt).
patterns.avoid: Write the payload to the child's stdin (or to a temp file and pass its path). Cap and validate anything that still has to go in argv.
patterns.counterexample: NOT a finding when the argument is provably short (a flag, an id, a single bounded token).

patterns.title: One failing iteration aborts the whole loop
patterns.symptom: A batch job iterating over projects, files or API calls dies on the first bad item; the remaining work is silently skipped and the run reports a single traceback instead of 40 successes and 1 failure.
patterns.detect: for/foreach body doing I/O (network, subprocess, file, DB) with no try/except (or try/catch) inside the loop; error handling wrapped around the loop instead of within it.
patterns.avoid: Wrap the loop body: record the failure per item, continue, and report a summary of failures at the end with a non-zero exit code if any occurred.
patterns.counterexample: NOT a finding when the items are genuinely dependent (each step consumes the previous one's output) and continuing would produce corrupt results.
